topic: A lending service has to count the people it cannot reach
grammarFocus: 学术论证的限定、因果、对比与证据范围
title: A lending service has to count the people it cannot reach
instructions: 原创学术微训练；场景、机构与数值均为虚构模拟，不是事实报道或官方试题。先独立阅读答题，再用原句核对限定、比较与因果。短篇专项不能替代完整陌生测评。
passage:
A. A fictional library began lending tools as well as books. Early publicity showed a rise in loans from forty in the first month to one hundred in the third. The project coordinator welcomed the demand but resisted calling the scheme accessible to the whole community. A transaction count showed use by borrowers; it said little about residents who could not borrow.

B. Membership required proof of a local address. That rule was familiar from book lending, yet it excluded people in temporary accommodation whose documents were incomplete. Collection hours created a second barrier. Tools were available only until five in the afternoon, when many residents were still at work. The coordinator kept a record of unsuccessful requests rather than treating them as evidence of no demand.

C. Equipment also differed in how easily it could be used. A compact drill could be carried on foot, while a heavy cleaning machine required transport. A list of available items did not reveal whether a household could take them home. To investigate, staff asked applicants about collection difficulties and offered a trial delivery service on two Saturdays. Requests increased, but the additional staffing cost had to be included in the evaluation.

D. Some members wanted to judge success by the value of tools borrowed. That measure would favour expensive equipment even if it helped few households. Others proposed the number of first-time borrowers, which would highlight reach but ignore repeated practical benefit. Neither indicator alone described the entire purpose of the service. The coordinator recommended reporting both and explaining their different meanings.

E. The review led to an evening collection session and a clearer process for applicants without standard documents. It did not remove every barrier, and the delivery trial was too short to justify a permanent expansion. By recording unmet requests alongside completed loans, the library made its next decisions more informed. Increased borrowing was a positive result, but a convincing account of access required attention to the people missing from the transaction log.
